results.summary: CORA-16 is a simple 16-bit CPU that uses external SPI memory for instruction fetch and execution. It provides an 8-bit general-purpose input and output bus, and supports single-stepping for debugging via a step pin. Status pins indicate busy, halt, and trap conditions, with trap recovery possible by stepping. The design requires an external SPI RAM and can be tested using a Raspberry Pi for emulation.

This project implements two independent byte-width double-ended queues (deques) using flip-flop arrays with pointers. Each deque can operate as a stack or queue depending on the end_select signal, and provides empty and full status flags. Push, pop, and replace operations are controlled via multiplexed inputs, and the end of the deque can be read from the data output. External hardware is not strictly required, but the design is intended to interface with other devices that can benefit from deque functionality.

CSIT-Luks is a camera lighting settings recommender that takes ISO, shutter speed, and focal ratio inputs via a rotary encoder and displays them on a four-digit seven-segment display. It reads an external luxmeter over SPI and uses the values to look up a recommended setting from a LUT stored in SPI flash, then displays the result. The design requires external hardware including a rotary encoder, seven-segment display, SPI luxmeter, and SPI flash. It is a practical tool for photography, though no silicon test results are provided.

This project is a prototype that simulates an image sensor to validate a readout method, converting light levels to frequencies and then measuring them with frequency counters. It includes testbenches for both a full 1MP sensor and a smaller pixel array, and is intended to be tested on fabricated hardware using an external RP2040 microcontroller. The design is not an actual image sensor but a test chip for readout circuitry. The documentation notes that the design may not be useful to others, but provides test instructions.

This is a 4-bit ALU implementing the Cornell University ECE2300 instruction set, with operations including addition, subtraction, shifts, AND, and OR. It takes two 4-bit inputs (A and B) and a 3-bit function select, and outputs a 4-bit result along with carry, overflow, negative, and zero flags. The design requires no external hardware beyond input and output connections. It is an educational project from a university course.

The Die Roller generates a pseudo-random number between 1 and a user-specified die size (up to 99) when a roll input is triggered. It uses a clock counter for randomness and displays the result on a dual seven-segment display via a PMOD output splitter. Silicon testing revealed that while the die size can be set and displayed, rolling the die does not show the result, indicating a functional issue. The design requires external PMOD hardware for display.

This project implements an 8-bit FIR filter with two coefficients, designed to filter unwanted frequencies from a digital signal. It uses shift registers to load the input signal and coefficients, then performs multiply-accumulate operations to produce the filtered output. The design was limited to two coefficients due to chip capacity, but includes comments for future expansion to four coefficients. Testing is done via a testbench, and no external hardware is specified.

This project is a simple display test that interfaces with a character LCD, based on a Wokwi project. It outputs data and control signals to drive the LCD, requiring external hardware in the form of a character LCD. The documentation is minimal, indicating it is just a test with no further details on functionality or testing. No silicon results are provided.

This is an 8-bit combinational multiply and divide unit that supports both signed and unsigned operations. It uses a clock to load input registers and provides immediate or registered output modes, with error flags for division overflow and divide-by-zero. The design is implemented in SpinalHDL and requires an external RP2040 for testing. Documentation is limited, with testing instructions deferred to a later date.

This project is an 8-bit combinational multiply and divide unit similar to the previous one, but implemented with sky130 high-availability and full-adder standard cells. It supports signed and unsigned operations and provides immediate or registered output modes with error flags. The design is in SpinalHDL and expects an RP2040 for testing. Documentation is sparse, with testing instructions to be provided later.
